subject: Dedicated capacity tenure safeguard & GPU price sensitivity — Acme Health
messages:
From: Jose Santos <j.santos@acmehealth.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity proposal — pricing sensitivity and safeguards

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed. We're ready to move the conversation to commercial terms. I've attached three commit scenarios (12/24/36 months) with our expected throughput and preferred SKU mix. The key ask from procurement is clarity on how Redwood will handle GPU market volatility over a multi-year commitment.

Specifically:
- What discount levers are available at different tenors and commitment sizes?
- Can we include a GPU-cost indexation clause (cap/floor) instead of an open pass-through?
- If GPU spot/wholesale costs spike >25% year-over-year, do you offer rebates, credits, or model fallback guarantees?

We'd prefer a 24–36 month tenor but need guardrails so our CFO is comfortable with the NPV. Can you send a proposal with (1) explicit discount tiers, (2) language options for GPU price protection, and (3) an illustration of worst-case monthly cost under each scenario?

Attachments: Acme_Commit_Scenarios_v3.xlsx (workbook)

Thanks,
Jose Santos
Director, Vendor Ops — Acme Health
procurement@acmehealth.com
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Jose Santos <j.santos@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal — pricing sensitivity and safeguards

Hi Jose — really appreciate the clear asks and the file.

High level: Redwood can support tiered discounts by committed monthly GPU hours and by SKU mix, plus two practical approaches to market volatility:

Option A — Indexation with caps/floors:
- Monthly invoice adjusts by a GPU-market index (public benchmark), capped at +/- 15% year-over-year; floor at -5% to protect minimum pricing.
- Suitable for 24–36 month tenors; predictable hedge but requires simple monthly reconciliation.

Option B — Fixed-rate + rebate escrow:
- We lock a fixed per-token/per-hour price for the commit and place a portion of the discount into an escrow. If global GPU wholesale prices spike >25% YoY, Redwood applies the escrow as targeted rebates over subsequent invoices.
- More cost-predictable for procurement; slightly higher list price than pure indexation.

Attached is a short proposal summary that maps your scenarios to our standard starters and an initial commercial suggestion for a 24-month commit (Scenario B preferred by our sales/finance team). The attached also includes a sample worst-case cost table assuming a 30% GPU cost shock.

Next steps:
- Would you be open to a 45-minute call Friday to walk through the two options and agree on triggers?
- If you prefer, we can push a redline-ready clause for your legal team to review after the call.

Attachments: redwood-proposal-summary.pdf

Best,
Chloe Martin
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 23 May 2028 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity proposal — pricing sensitivity and safeguards

Folks — forwarding Acme's ask and my initial proposal. TL;DR: Acme prefers 24–36 months and wants a clear GPU-price guardrail. I sketched two commercial approaches (indexation w/ cap/floor OR fixed-rate + rebate escrow). Need alignment on allowable discount depth and an approval path for >standard concession.

Key numbers I propose to present: (all illustrative, see attached spreadsheet)
- 24-month, 2.5M GPU-hour commit: base discount 18% off list; with a rebate escrow -> net effective discount structure ~15% if no shocks.
- 36-month, 4.0M GPU-hour commit: base discount 23% off list; indexation cap/floor +/-15% YoY.

Questions for pricing/finance:
1) Marcus — are we comfortable with an initial 23% list discount for the 36mo bucket if we require index cap/floor? Any appetite to convert part of that into usage-based credits instead of up-front reduction?
2) Laura — finance will need a simple NPV comparison; can you model both options (indexation w/ cap vs escrow rebate) with a +30% GPU-cost shock scenario?
3) Rishi — product needs to confirm our fallback model variants (smaller quantized model or higher-latency SKU) and SLO/throughput guarantees if GPU supply gets constrained.

Attachments: Acme_Commit_Scenarios_v3.xlsx (original)

On Marcus's point, I agree that a rebate/escrow reduces our upfront margin erosion and is easier to reconcile. I'd like to propose Redwood hold 40% of the incremental discount in escrow for 12 months if a market spike occurs, then release as rebate to the customer.

Please reply inline with approvals or edits — I need to get back to Jose with a final recommended commercial structure by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Chloe

- Prefer rebates over retroactive invoice credits to keep admin low.
- Approve up to 20% base discount for 36mo only with escrow guardrail; anything beyond 20% requires VP approval.

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>

Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 24 May 2028 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Final commercial recommendation & next steps — Acme 24mo proposal

Jose — thanks for the time on Friday. Per the internal alignment above, here's Redwood's recommended path and the language we'll put in the term sheet:

1) Tenor & Commitment: 24-month reserved capacity, 2.6M committed GPU hours across prioritized SKUs.
2) Pricing: 20% base discount off list for the 24-month commit. 3% of ARR held in rebate escrow (capped at 6 months of committed revenue).
3) GPU protection trigger: If verified GPU wholesale index (Bloomberg GPU Index, or alternate agreed benchmark) increases >25% YoY, Redwood will apply escrow rebates on a pro rata basis across the following 12 months.
4) Fallbacks & SLOs: Redwood will provide a quantized fallback model (medium) with a targeted latency increase no greater than 30% and a migration window of 10 days. We will include automatic routing to alternative SKUs only after both parties agree the trigger threshold is met.

I've attached the SKU breakdown and a revised proposal summary for your legal and procurement teams. If that aligns, I'll send a DocuSign with the term sheet and the escrow appendix for signature.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sku-breakdown.pdf, redwood-proposal-summary.pdf
